title: CompTIA Security+ (SY0-801)
summary: CompTIA Security+ is the vendor-neutral baseline certification for defensive security work, and SY0-801 is the newer exam version that replaces SY0-701. This page tracks the SY0-801 edition: the lab set is published, and its exercise batches are being written against the same five domains so practice and reading stay aligned.
objectives: General Security Concepts: controls, the CIA triad, authentication and authorisation, change management and cryptographic solutions.
Threats, Vulnerabilities and Mitigations: threat actors and vectors, vulnerability classes, malicious activity and the controls that reduce exposure.
Security Architecture: secure design, cloud and virtualisation, resilience and the placement of network security controls.
Security Operations: monitoring and alerting, logging, identity administration, automation and operational hardening.
Security Program Management and Oversight: risk management, third-party risk, compliance, auditing and security awareness.
attributionNote: Summary written from publicly available CompTIA Security+ material. Cyber Pulse Academy is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by CompTIA.

beginner.definition: Security+ is a well-known entry-level security certificate from CompTIA. SY0-801 is the newer version of that exam, and this page covers the newer one.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many entry security jobs ask for Security+. Practising here uses the same five domains as the exam version you are sitting, so the labs and the batches you open match the certificate you are studying for.
howItWorks: You study five domains: general concepts, threats and mitigations, architecture, operations, and programme management.
Each domain is a chapter on this page, and each lab sits under the section it belongs to.
The labs are simulations: you read an artefact, choose an action, and see why it was right.
Exercise batches for the sections are being written and will appear beside the labs.
beginner.example: Think of a building walkthrough: not the locksmith, but the person with the clipboard checking that doors lock, cameras record, and the fire plan exists.
takeaways: Security+ proves broad security basics rather than depth in one product.
SY0-801 is the current exam version; this page tracks that edition.
The labs are playable now; the graded batches follow.

chapters.title: General Security Concepts
objectives: 1.1 Compare and contrast various types of security controls
1.2 Demonstrate the impact of change management processes on security
1.3 Explain the importance of using appropriate cryptographic solutions

chapters.title: Threats, Vulnerabilities and Mitigations
objectives: 2.1 Compare and contrast common threat actors and motivations
2.2 Explain common threat vectors and attack surfaces
2.3 Analyze indicators of malicious activity
2.4 Examine common vulnerabilities and associated risks
2.5 Explain the security risks associated with artificial intelligence (AI)

chapters.title: Security Architecture
objectives: 3.1 Compare and contrast security implications of different architecture models
3.2 Apply security principles to secure enterprise infrastructure
3.3 Understand concepts related to data protection
3.4 Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architectures

chapters.title: Security Operations
objectives: 4.1 Apply common security techniques to computing resources
4.2 Explain asset management concepts and practices
4.3 Analyze indicators of vulnerabilities and implement appropriate mitigation strategies
4.4 Describe security monitoring and alerting concepts
4.5 Manage identity and access controls
4.6 Explain the importance of automation and orchestration in security operations
4.7 Implement incident response activities
4.8 Use data sources to support investigations

chapters.title: Security Program Management and Oversight
objectives: 5.1 Define elements of an effective security governance program
5.2 Manage security risk management processes and concepts
5.3 Explain third-party risk management concepts
5.4 Support security compliance and privacy considerations
5.5 Compare and contrast audits and assessments
5.6 Promote security awareness practices
